items.question: What do you need from me to get started?
items.answer: A brief overview of your product, reference images or CAD files if available, the intended use of the visuals, and any brand or creative direction you already have. From there, the scope and production plan can be shaped clearly.

items.question: Which file formats can I provide?
items.answer: Common CAD, 3D, vector, and image formats can be used. STEP, IGES, OBJ, FBX, STL, AI, PDF, PNG, and high-resolution product photography are all useful starting points depending on the project.

items.question: How long does a project usually take?
items.answer: Timelines depend on the number of products, complexity, revisions, and final deliverables. A focused rendering project may take several days, while larger animation or campaign packages may require multiple weeks.

items.question: Can you create visuals before the product is manufactured?
items.answer: Yes. Product visuals can be created from CAD files, sketches, measurements, prototypes, or detailed references, making 3D rendering especially useful for launches, investor presentations, and pre-production marketing.

items.question: How many revisions are included?
items.answer: The revision allowance is agreed before work begins and depends on the project scope. Each stage is reviewed at sensible checkpoints so feedback stays organized and major changes do not arrive after final production.
